last.verdict: MetLife posted its best quarterly adjusted earnings per share ever, helped by a jump in investment returns, with revenue growing in every segment.

takeaways.label: Record profit, partly investment-driven
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to $2.85, excluding one-time items. Returns from variable investments such as private equity jumped 49% to $720 million, a swing-prone source of earnings.

takeaways.label: Growth across the business
takeaways.text: Revenue excluding large pension deals grew 8% to $13.5 billion, with growth in all six segments. Europe, Middle East and Africa earnings rose 30% excluding one-time items.

takeaways.label: Retirement unit held back
takeaways.text: Retirement and Income Solutions earnings fell 6% after a $65 million hit from the annual review of insurance assumptions. Excluding it, earnings rose 12%.

takeaways.label: Returns and cash
takeaways.text: Return on equity was 19.6% excluding one-time items. About $1 billion went back to shareholders, and MetLife says it is on track for its yearly free cash flow and expense targets.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
